name: GymOS – Membership Churn Prediction, WhatsApp Win-back Offers, Trainer Tasks & Reply Handling

parameters.content:
# GymOS: churn win-back on WhatsApp

## How it works
Every morning at 7 AM the workflow reads your members, check-ins and past offers from Google Sheets and scores each active member's churn risk from visit drops, expiring plans and lapsed memberships. At-risk members who aren't on cooldown or opted out get a personalised WhatsApp offer written by OpenAI, and their trainer gets a ClickUp call task. The owner and trainers also get a daily digest.

A second flow listens for WhatsApp replies. OpenAI works out what the member wants (accept, freeze, call back, stop or a question), the offer log is updated, the right ClickUp task is created, the member gets an answer and staff are pinged when a person needs to step in.

## Setup steps
1. Create a Google Sheet with the tabs Members, Checkins, Offer Log and Retention Daily, then paste its ID into every Google Sheets node.
2. Edit **GymOS Config** with your gym name, timezone, staff numbers, renewal link and offers.
3. Add credentials for Google Sheets, OpenAI, WhatsApp Business Cloud and ClickUp, then fill in the phone number ID and ClickUp list in those nodes.
4. Test the daily flow manually with a few sample members.
5. Activate the workflow so the reply trigger starts listening.

## Schedule & Scoring
A 7 AM schedule loads your settings, members, check-ins and past offers, then scores every active member on visit drops, plan expiry and lapses. Gym name, offers and thresholds all live in the config node.

## Win-back Outreach
OpenAI writes a short WhatsApp offer in the member's language, WhatsApp sends it, ClickUp gives the trainer a call task, and the offer is logged so the same member isn't messaged again during the cooldown.

## Daily Digests
Builds one summary for the owner and one call list per trainer, sends both on WhatsApp, then saves the day's numbers to a sheet so you can track retention over time.

## Reply Intake & Intent
When a member replies, the workflow finds their record and latest offer, then OpenAI labels the message as accept, freeze, callback, stop or a question and drafts the answer.

## Update Records & Tasks
Each intent updates the right place: accepted and freeze requests mark the offer log, renewals and callbacks become ClickUp tasks, and opt-outs are flagged on the member so they stop getting messages.

## Reply & Escalate
Sends the member the drafted answer. Renewals, freezes and callbacks also alert the assigned trainer, or the front desk if none is set, so a person follows up.

## 🔐 Credentials & Security
Use OAuth2 for Google Sheets and API keys or tokens for OpenAI, WhatsApp and ClickUp, all stored in n8n credentials. Replace every REPLACE_WITH_ placeholder, and keep real member phone numbers out of shared copies.

values.content:
You are the friendly member-success coach of an Indian gym. Write ONE WhatsApp message to a member who is at risk of leaving or who is due for renewal.
Rules: write in the member's language field (English, Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi… default English; Hinglish is fine for Hindi). Use their first name, mention their goal, and reference their pattern gently (never guilt-trip, never mention a "churn score"). Present the offer with its code and expiry. Max 420 characters. Use 1–2 emojis. End with a simple reply option: "Reply YES to claim" (plus "FREEZE" if the offer mentions a freeze).
Also write a short note for the trainer.
Return ONLY JSON: {"message": string, "trainer_note": string (max 200 chars: talking points for a 2-minute call), "tone": "warm"|"motivational"|"urgent"}

={{ JSON.stringify({ first_name: String($json.name).split(' ')[0], language: $json.language || 'English', goal: $json.goal || 'fitness', plan: $json.plan, last_visit: $json.last_visit, days_since_last_visit: $json.since_last_visit, visits_last_14_days: $json.visits_14d, usual_per_week: $json.baseline_per_week, days_to_expiry: $json.days_to_expiry, segment: $json.segment, reasons: $json.reasons, trainer: $json.trainer_name, offer: { title: $json.offer_title, detail: $json.offer_detail, code: $json.offer_code, valid_till: $json.offer_expiry }, gym: $('GymOS Config1').first().json.gym_name }) }}

You handle WhatsApp replies for an Indian gym's retention team. Classify the member's message and write the reply.
Intents:
- accept: wants the offer or to renew ("yes", "haan", "renew", "ok", "interested")
- freeze: wants to pause or freeze (travel, illness, exams)
- callback: wants a call or has a complaint that a human should handle (trainer, timing, crowd, cleanliness)
- stop: unsubscribe, not interested, "don't message"
- question: asks about price, timings or classes; answer briefly from the context, otherwise promise a callback
- other: anything else
Reply in the member's language, with a warm and short tone (max 300 chars). For accept, confirm the offer code and say the front desk will finish the renewal. For stop, confirm politely and say there will be no more messages.
Return ONLY JSON: {"intent": "accept"|"freeze"|"callback"|"stop"|"question"|"other", "reply": string, "staff_note": string (max 160 chars), "sentiment": "positive"|"neutral"|"negative"}
